transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brings me in... I guess I've just completely stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. Like, I haven't even been walking into my shop lately just to enjoy the smell of the wood. And I usually love that smell. I've been a carpenter a long time, and there's nothing quite like the scent of fresh cut cedar or mahogany. I was actually working on a cedar chest for my niece's wedding—she got married up in Portland a few weeks ago. Beautiful outdoor ceremony, though it rained right at the end. You know how the weather is up there, you can't ever trust a clear sky. Her new husband is a nice enough guy, works in IT or something with computers. I don't really understand how a man can spend all day just staring at a screen, to be honest with you. 

But anyway, I just... I don't have the drive for my shop anymore. Or for anything else, really. I've stopped going to my salsa nights, haven't been to the church gatherings at all. I usually cook for the neighbors, too. I always make this big batch of smoked brisket or chili for the block. Mrs. Higgins next door always returns my Tupperware with a little slice of lemon pound cake—she's a sweet lady, lost her husband a few years back. But yeah, I just haven't had it in me to fire up the smoker or see anyone. I just don't care about doing any of it anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way, without the drive to do the things you usually enjoy?

Well, let's see... I'd say it’s been about two months. This whole change in my mood, just not wanting to do anything at all, it really started about two months ago when my wife’s health suddenly declined. It was real sudden, and it just completely wrecked our daily routine. We used to have things so set, you know? Like, every morning we’d sit on the back porch with our coffee. I always drink mine black, but she likes that sweet vanilla creamer stuff. I keep telling her all that sugar isn't good for her, especially with how expensive groceries are getting. Have you been to the store lately? The price of eggs is just unbelievable. I actually thought about getting some chickens for the backyard, building a nice little coop for them. I’ve got plenty of good pine left over from a job I did for the Hendersons down the street. Nice folks, the Hendersons. They have this golden retriever that used to steal my tape measure right off my tool belt... but anyway, yeah. About two months since she got sick and our routine went out the window.
Are you still able to experience pleasure when you do happen to engage in these activities, even if you don't feel like doing them?

No, not really. Even if I force myself to go out to the shop, it's just... nothing. Like I said before, I used to love just walking in there for the smell of the wood. That's why I'm here, honestly. I've completely stopped wanting to do the things that keep me going. The salsa nights, the church gatherings, cooking for the neighbors... it's all just gone flat. 

I actually tried to go to church a few weeks ago, thinking it might help. Pastor Dave was giving a sermon on patience, I think. He's a good speaker, usually. He used to be a used car salesman before he found his calling, which always struck me as funny. You know, going from selling lemons to saving souls. He actually sold me a '98 Ford F-150 back in the day. Good truck. Ran for almost two hundred thousand miles before the transmission finally gave out on me while I was hauling a load of drywall up I-5. The tow truck driver who picked me up was this young kid, couldn't have been more than twenty, listening to that loud electronic music. I asked him how he could concentrate on driving with all that noise, and he just laughed. But anyway, yeah... even when I try to do those things now, I just don't get any joy out of them at all.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or how quickly you're able to perform daily tasks?

Well, yeah, my energy is just shot. It's like... even if I've been sitting down all day or I've had a full night in bed, my body just feels completely worn out. It feels exactly like I've been up on a ladder framing a roof for ten hours straight in the July heat. You know how that sun beats down on you when you're up high like that? There's no shade, nowhere to hide. I used to work on this crew with a guy named Tommy, and Tommy would always bring these huge jugs of iced tea. Not the sweet kind, just plain black tea with a ton of lemon. He said the sugar made you crash harder. He ended up moving out to Arizona, said the dry heat was better for his joints. I don't know how anyone can stand living in a desert, honestly. All that sand and those cactus things... what do they call them? Saguaro? Yeah, those big ones with the arms. 

But anyway, yeah, I'm just so tired all the time now. Even just doing small chores, like loading my tools into the back of the truck, it just feels like it's way too much effort. I look at my toolbelt and I just can't even fathom picking it up.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you were dead?

Well... yeah, I guess I have. I mean, I've had these thoughts lately where I just think... maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up at all. It's awful to say out loud, but sometimes I even catch myself thinking that my wife and my family might actually be better off without me dragging them down. Which really scares me, to be honest. I've never been the kind of guy to think like that. My dad, he was a tough old bird, Korean War vet. He used to say that a man's job was to stand strong no matter what the wind was doing. He had this old oak tree in the front yard that got hit by lightning back in '85. Split right down the middle, but half of it kept growing anyway. He refused to cut it down. Said it earned the right to stay. The city kept sending him letters about it being a hazard, but he just threw them right in the trash. He was stubborn like that. We used to sit under that half-tree and he'd tell me stories about his unit. But... yeah, those thoughts about not waking up, they've been creeping in and it just doesn't feel like me at all.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or weight over the past two months?

No, not really. My appetite's been about the same, I guess. I still eat my regular meals. My wife makes sure of that, bless her. She makes this incredible pot roast on Sundays. Slow-cooks it all day with carrots and potatoes. The secret, she says, is searing the meat first in a cast iron skillet. We've had that same skillet since we got married thirty years ago. Found it at a garage sale for five bucks. Best five bucks I ever spent. The guy selling it was moving out to Florida to retire. Had a whole collection of vintage fishing gear he was trying to get rid of, too. I almost bought a bamboo fly rod from him, but I've never really been much of a fisherman. Always seemed like too much sitting around waiting for something to happen. I prefer working with my hands, you know? Making something solid. But yeah, to answer your question, no, my weight hasn't changed or anything like that.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating or making decisions over the past two months?

Yeah, it's been real tough. I'll be looking at blueprints, right? Blueprints I've read my whole life, same kind of schematics I've been working off of for thirty years. And the lines just blur together in my head. I can't make heads or tails of it. I end up having to ask the younger guys on the crew to repeat things I should understand right away. It's embarrassing, really. Speaking of the younger guys, we got this new kid, Mike. Good kid, but he wears these bright neon yellow work boots. I don't know where he found them, but you can see him coming from a mile away. I told him he looks like a walking traffic cone, but he says they're the most comfortable boots he's ever owned. He actually bought them online. I don't trust buying shoes online, you know? You gotta try them on, walk around the store a bit, make sure they don't pinch your toes. My wife buys all her shoes online now, but she's always having to send them back because they don't fit right. It just seems like a hassle to me, boxing them back up, taking them to the post office... the line at our post office is always out the door. But anyway, yeah, my brain just feels like it's in a fog, can't focus on the plans at all.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual over the past two months?

Yeah, the guys at the job site have been on my case about it. They say half the time I'm moving like my boots are full of wet cement, taking forever just to pick up a single board. Which, actually, I really did get my boots stuck in wet cement once. Back in '98, we were doing this big driveway pour for a guy who owned a car dealership. He wanted this fancy stamped concrete, paid a fortune for it. Well, the kid running the screed board tripped and I had to jump right in the mix to catch it before he ruined the grade. Ruined a perfectly good pair of Red Wing boots. You can't just wash that stuff off once it starts to cure, you know, it just eats right through the leather. I tried taking them to a cobbler, this old Italian guy downtown, but he just took one look and laughed at me. His shop smelled amazing, though, like shoe polish and strong espresso. He had this antique brass cash register that must have weighed two hundred pounds. But anyway, yeah, if I'm not moving in slow motion, it's the other way around. I'll just get stuck pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands together over and over, and not actually doing anything useful at all.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Yeah, I mean, like I was just saying a minute ago, right? That's exactly what I meant about pacing around the shop. I get real restless and just walk back and forth, rubbing my hands together, not actually doing a damn thing useful. 

Speaking of my hands, though, my knuckles have been absolutely killing me lately. I think it's the weather changing. We had that huge cold front move in last Tuesday. Reminds me of the winter of '14. Man, it got so cold that year the pipes actually froze solid in our main shop. We had to rent these massive propane torpedo heaters just to keep the guys from freezing to death. You gotta be real careful with those things, though, if you don't ventilate right. My buddy Dave used to run one in his garage with the door shut tight, gave himself mild carbon monoxide poisoning. He's fine now, but they kept him overnight at the hospital for observation. He complained the whole time about the food. Said they just gave him green Jell-O and a piece of dry meatloaf. I never understood why hospitals always push Jell-O on you. Is it supposed to be medicinal or something? My wife makes this cherry Jell-O mold for Thanksgiving with the little mandarin oranges inside, but that's a whole different ballgame. 

But yeah, to answer you, it's just like I mentioned before—I get stuck in that pacing rut, just fidgeting and walking in circles instead of working.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything in particular lately?

Yeah, I have. I mean, it's just heavy on my chest all the time. I keep replaying every single doctor's appointment, every little change in my wife's health... I just keep telling myself that a better husband would have caught it sooner, you know? Like I should have protected her somehow. 

We used to go to this doctor, Dr. Henderson. Nice guy, had these old Norman Rockwell paintings in his waiting room. I always liked the one with the kid at the soda fountain. You don't see soda fountains anymore, do you? When I was a kid, my granddad used to take me to the pharmacy down on Main Street and they had a real marble counter. We'd get these cherry phosphates. Best thing I ever tasted. Granddad was a carpenter, too, actually. Taught me how to hold a hammer when I was just five years old. He built this incredible oak dining table for my grandmother that we still have in our house. Weighs an absolute ton. We tried moving it when we repainted the dining room last spring, and I swear I almost threw my back out. We painted it this color called "Sea Salt," which my wife picked out. She loves those coastal colors. Reminds her of our honeymoon in Cape Cod. We ate so much lobster on that trip I thought I was gonna turn red. 

But yeah, I just... I can't stop thinking that if I'd paid closer attention, maybe she wouldn't be going through all this, and it's my fault I didn't see the signs.
Have you noticed yourself speaking more slowly than usual over the past two months?

Yeah, I think I already mentioned that a minute ago, didn't I? The guys at the site are always on my case about it. They say I'm moving like my boots are full of wet cement, like it takes me forever just to pick up a single piece of lumber. 

Speaking of lumber, the price of pine has gone absolutely through the roof lately. I went down to the supplier last week, and I couldn't believe it. I told the guy, "Are these boards lined with gold?" He just laughed, but it's no joke when you're trying to bid a job. Used to be you could build a whole deck for what they're charging for a stack of two-by-fours now. My buddy Frank builds these massive wrap-around porches out in the county, and he's had to start using this composite decking material instead. It looks okay, I guess, but it doesn't have the same feel as real wood. Real wood has a soul, you know? You can smell the sap when you cut into it. My grandfather used to say you could tell a lot about a man by how he treated his tools and his timber. He kept his chisels so sharp you could shave with them. He had this old leather strop hanging by his workbench... 

But anyway, yeah, they say I'm talking and moving way slower than normal. Unless I'm doing the opposite and just pacing around the shop rubbing my hands together, getting absolutely nothing done.
Have you been feeling like you're moving more quickly than usual, or like your thoughts are racing?

Yeah, well, before this whole cement-boots feeling set in, I had this crazy surge going on. I literally could not sit still. I was up late into the night, just sketching out all these new workshop ideas, calling up suppliers, and hunting for the next thing to fix before I had even finished the first project. 

Speaking of sketching, I still use those old-school yellow Dixon Ticonderoga pencils. Number twos. You know the ones? The eraser on those things is actually decent. Most pencils nowadays, the eraser just smudges the graphite everywhere and ruins the paper. I buy them by the gross from this little office supply store downtown. The guy who runs it, Mr. Higgins, he’s been there since the eighties. He’s got this massive collection of vintage typewriters in the back of the shop. Really beautiful machines. Underwood, Royal, Smith Corona. He let me type on this 1930s Underwood once, and the keys take so much force to press down, your fingers actually get a workout. Makes you appreciate modern keyboards, even if they feel cheap and plasticky. My grandson has this mechanical keyboard for his computer games that lights up in all these crazy rainbow colors. Looks like a disco in his bedroom. I don't get the appeal of playing games in the dark like that, honestly. It's gotta be terrible for your eyes. My mom used to yell at me for reading comics by flashlight under the covers when I was a kid... 

But anyway, yeah. I was just running on that surge, jumping from one fix-it job to the next without finishing anything.
Would you say that your feelings of guilt are interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Yeah, I'd say it is. It's just... I can't focus on the work anymore. I've actually had to hand off parts of jobs that I normally supervise myself, which is hard for me because I like things done a certain way. 

Like when we're framing a house, if the studs aren't perfectly plumb, it throws off the drywall, and then the baseboards don't sit right. It's a whole domino effect. I learned that from this old foreman I worked under when I was first starting out, guy named Sal. Sal was a character. Always had an unlit cigar in his mouth, just chewing on it all day long. Said he quit smoking in '85 but missed the feel of it. He drove this beat-up old Ford F-150 that was more rust than metal. The tailgate wouldn't even latch, so he had it held shut with a bungee cord. I remember one time we were driving down I-95 and that cord snapped, and all his empty coffee cups just went flying out the back like confetti. He drank that cheap diner coffee, the kind that tastes like burnt pennies. We used to go to this diner on 4th Street, Tommy's. They had the best meatloaf sandwich I've ever had in my life. Thick slice of meatloaf, melted provolone, crispy onions on toasted sourdough. My wife makes a good meatloaf, but she puts green peppers in hers. I'm not a fan of green peppers. They overpower everything else in the dish, you know?

But yeah, the guilt is just... it's bad. I've pulled away from everyone. Haven't been to church in weeks, ignoring my friends, the neighbors... It got so bad that my wife and the contact from our parish actually got really worried about my safety.
Do you feel like you're a burden to your family and friends most of the time?

Yeah, I do. I really do. I've been having these thoughts lately, like... maybe it would just be easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. Sometimes I catch myself thinking my wife and the kids might actually be better off without me dragging them down, even though thinking that way really scares me. 

Speaking of sleeping, we bought this new mattress a couple months ago, one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box. You cut the plastic and it just inflates like a life raft. It's supposed to be great for your back, but honestly, I think I liked our old coil spring mattress better. We had that thing for fifteen years. I bought it at this local furniture store that used to be over on Main Street, right next to the old movie theater. The theater shut down back in the nineties, but they still have the marquee up. They used to show double features on Saturdays for three bucks. I took my wife there on our first date, actually. We saw some terrible sci-fi movie about giant ants or something, I don't even remember the name of it. We shared a large popcorn, and she accidentally spilled half of it on the floor when a rat ran across the aisle. She screamed so loud the projectionist actually stopped the film. We still laugh about that. Popcorn at the movies is a total rip-off now anyway. You go in there and they want ten dollars for a bucket of stale corn and fake butter. I started sneaking in my own snacks in my coat pockets. The kids think it's embarrassing, but I refuse to pay those prices. My daughter, she's in college now, she told me they check your bags at the door at the theater near her campus...

But yeah, I do feel like a burden. Thinking they'd be better off if I wasn't around, it just... it creeps in, you know?
Would you say your feelings of worthlessness are present nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much every day. It's like this heavy weight, you know? I just... I keep replaying every single doctor's appointment, every little change in my wife’s health over the last few years. I keep telling myself that a better husband would have caught it sooner, or... or protected her somehow. 

She used to love going to those antique fairs on the weekends before she got sick. We'd drive out to the county fairgrounds, usually on a Sunday morning. The traffic out there on Route 9 is always a nightmare because of the farmers' market they set up right off the highway. People just slam on their brakes to turn in for fresh tomatoes. I don't get it, honestly. You can buy perfectly good tomatoes at the Stop & Shop down the street. Although, I will say, the supermarket tomatoes always taste kind of watery compared to the ones my grandfather used to grow. He had this massive garden in his backyard. Grew tomatoes, cucumbers, zucchini the size of baseball bats. He used to make his own pickles in these giant glass jars he kept in the cellar. The cellar always smelled like dill and damp earth. I hated going down there as a kid because there were these huge wolf spiders that would hang out near the water heater. I’m still terrified of spiders. Last week I saw one in the garage near my workbench, right next to my circular saw. I actually left the garage and didn't go back in for two days. My son had to come over and kill it for me. He laughed at me, of course. Kids always think they're tougher than their old man once they hit their twenties...

But yeah, the worthlessness... it's there every day. Just constantly thinking I failed her when she needed me most.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities and feelings of worthlessness are interfering with your ability to function at work or take care of things at home?

Yeah, definitely. Like I was saying before, I just... I can't focus on the work anymore. I've actually had to hand off parts of jobs that I normally supervise myself. And at home, I've just pulled away from everyone. Haven't been to church in weeks, ignoring my friends, the neighbors... It got so bad that my wife and the contact from our parish actually got really worried about my safety. 

It's funny, the guy from the parish, Father Mike, he used to be a carpenter too before he joined the priesthood. He's always asking me about the wood I use. He loves cherry wood. Personally, I think cherry is a little too soft for most structural stuff, but it finishes beautifully if you're making cabinets or something. I built a cherry wood hutch for my wife for our tenth anniversary. Took me three months of working weekends in the garage. I used this special tung oil finish that really brought out the grain. Tung oil is great, but it takes forever to dry. You have to apply a coat, wait twenty-four hours, sand it with steel wool, and then do it all over again. I think I put six coats on that hutch. The smell of the oil lingered in the garage for weeks. It kind of smells like roasted nuts, which I didn't mind, but the dog hated it. We had a Golden Retriever back then, Buster. Best dog in the world. He used to sleep under my workbench while I was out there. He hated thunderstorms, though. One time, the thunder was so loud he tried to hide under my truck and got himself stuck. I had to jack up the back end just to get him out... 

But yeah, I'm just not functioning right now. Work, home, it's all just falling apart.
Do you feel like your symptoms have been consistently worse over the past two weeks?

Yeah, it's been bad for a while now. Not just two weeks. It's been dragging on for about six months now, honestly. It's definitely not just a bad week or normal stress anymore. Six months is a long time to feel like this. 

Six months ago was right around the time the transmission went out on my truck. It's a Ford F-150, 2015 model. Great truck, usually. I bought it used from a guy a few towns over who used it for his landscaping business, so it already had some miles on it, but the engine was solid. Anyway, the transmission just completely gave up on me while I was on the highway. Had to get it towed to this shop my brother-in-law recommended. The mechanic there, this guy named Sal, he's a real character. Always has a cigar stub in his mouth, even when he's under a car. I don't know how he breathes down there. He quoted me three grand to rebuild the transmission. Three grand! I thought about just buying a new truck, but have you seen the prices on new trucks lately? It's highway robbery. They put all these computers and touchscreens in them now. I don't need a touchscreen to haul lumber, you know? I just need a radio and a heater that works. My first truck was an old Chevy C10. Bare bones, manual roll-up windows. If something broke, you could actually fix it yourself with a wrench and some elbow grease. Now you need a computer degree just to change the oil... 

But yeah, the depression. It's been about six months of this heavy feeling. It's just... it's been a long six months.
Would you say that your symptoms have been consistently worse over the past two weeks?

Well, like I was just saying, doc, it's not just the last two weeks. It's been dragging on for about six months now. It's definitely been long enough that it no longer feels like just a bad week or ordinary stress, you know? 

Six months... yeah, that would've been right around the time my crew and I were finishing up the wrap-around deck on the Henderson place. Nice folks, the Hendersons. Mrs. Henderson would always bring us out these big pitchers of iced tea around noon. Not the cheap powdered stuff, either. She brewed it real strong with actual tea bags and put fresh mint in it. Said she grew the mint right there in her kitchen window box. Mint is funny like that, you know, it grows like an absolute weed if you aren't careful. My wife tried planting some in our backyard garden a few years back and it completely took over the whole bed. Choked the life right out of her beefsteak tomatoes. We had to dig up the dirt and start completely over the next spring. I bought this organic compost from a farm stand out in the valley to mix into the soil, and let me tell you, it smelled like absolute death. The dog loved it, though. He got out of the house and rolled right in it while I was grabbing my shovel. Had to give him three baths in the driveway with that oatmeal shampoo just to get the stink out. My back was killing me from leaning over the tub... 

But anyway, yeah, to answer your question, it's been a solid six months of this. Not just the last couple of weeks.
Would you say that your symptoms are severely impairing your ability to function in daily life?

Yeah, doc, I mean... I feel like we're going in circles here a bit, but yes. It's severely impairing everything. Like I mentioned before, I'm handing off jobs at work that I usually supervise myself. I just can't do it. And at home, I've completely pulled away. Haven't been to church, ignoring my friends, the neighbors... My wife and Father Mike got so worried about my safety that they had a whole intervention of sorts. 

Interventions are rough. Reminds me of when my brother-in-law, Gary, had to have an intervention for his gambling problem. This was back in the late nineties. Gary was a good guy, but he got hooked on those riverboat casinos. He'd drive three hours just to play blackjack on a Tuesday night. He lost his boat, his savings, almost lost his house. My sister was a wreck. We all sat around their living room—me, my wife, my sister, and Gary's old high school baseball coach, for some reason. Gary was furious. He stormed out and drove off in his Buick. Those old Buicks, they floated down the road like a boat. You couldn't feel a single bump. I always preferred a stiffer suspension, like on a truck, so you can actually feel the road, you know? You want to know what the tires are doing. If you're hauling a trailer full of drywall, you need to feel if it starts swaying. Drywall is heavy stuff, especially the half-inch fire-rated boards. You don't want to mess around with that... 

But anyway, yeah, the impairment is severe. Work, home, it's all a mess. I'm just not functioning.
Would you say that your current state is the worst you've felt in the past two months?

Well, to be honest with you doc, this whole... this whole specific change in my mood and my behavior, it's really been going on for about two months now. That's right around the time my wife's health suddenly declined and our whole daily routine just went completely out the window. 

It was a massive adjustment. We were suddenly having to drive back and forth to the medical center downtown for her, and let me tell you, the parking garage at that place is an absolute nightmare. I don't know who engineered it, but they designed it with these incredibly tight corners. I drive a full-size pickup, and trying to maneuver around those concrete pillars is like threading a needle in the dark. I actually scraped the passenger side mirror on one of those bright yellow barricade poles. Left a nasty paint streak right on the mirror housing. 

You know, you can usually get paint transfer like that off with a little rubbing compound and a good microfiber cloth if you catch it early enough. You just gotta use small, tight circular motions. You can't press too hard, though, or you'll burn right through the factory clear coat. A lot of guys make that exact mistake. They go out and buy those cheap orbital buffers from the hardware store and just go to town on their doors, and the next thing you know, they're looking at bare primer. Primer isn't meant to be exposed to the weather like that. It actually absorbs moisture, and then before you know it, you get rust bubbling up from underneath the paint... 

But anyway, yeah. Two months. Ever since her health took that sudden hit and our routine changed, my mood has just been stuck in this state.

I’ve got plenty of good pine left over from a job I did for the Hendersons down the street. Nice folks, the Hendersons. They have this golden retriever that used to steal my tape measure right off my tool belt... but anyway, yeah. About two months since she got sick and our routine went out the window.

doctor.intent: determine presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Are you still able to experience pleasure when you do happen to engage in these activities, even if you don't feel like doing them?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that I have stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going, like salsa nights, church gatherings, cooking for the neighbors, or even walking into my shop just to enjoy the smell of the wood.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about my ability to experience pleasure in activities, which directly relates to the loss of interest and pleasure symptom.

patient.answer:
No, not really. Even if I force myself to go out to the shop, it's just... nothing. Like I said before, I used to love just walking in there for the smell of the wood. That's why I'm here, honestly. I've completely stopped wanting to do the things that keep me going. The salsa nights, the church gatherings, cooking for the neighbors... it's all just gone flat. 

I actually tried to go to church a few weeks ago, thinking it might help. Pastor Dave was giving a sermon on patience, I think. He's a good speaker, usually. He used to be a used car salesman before he found his calling, which always struck me as funny. You know, going from selling lemons to saving souls. He actually sold me a '98 Ford F-150 back in the day. Good truck. Ran for almost two hundred thousand miles before the transmission finally gave out on me while I was hauling a load of drywall up I-5. The tow truck driver who picked me up was this young kid, couldn't have been more than twenty, listening to that loud electronic music. I asked him how he could concentrate on driving with all that noise, and he just laughed. But anyway, yeah... even when I try to do those things now, I just don't get any joy out of them at all.

inference.note: F32.4, F32.5, F32.8, F32.9 were ruled out due to the patient's description of a persistent loss of interest in activities and a depressed mood for two months, which is more indicative of a depressive episode.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of psychomotor retardation
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or how quickly you're able to perform daily tasks?

target_item.manifestation: Even after sitting down or getting a full night in bed, my body feels worn out like I have been framing a roof all day, and small chores like loading tools into the truck feel like too much.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, my energy is just shot. It's like... even if I've been sitting down all day or I've had a full night in bed, my body just feels completely worn out. It feels exactly like I've been up on a ladder framing a roof for ten hours straight in the July heat. You know how that sun beats down on you when you're up high like that? There's no shade, nowhere to hide. I used to work on this crew with a guy named Tommy, and Tommy would always bring these huge jugs of iced tea. Not the sweet kind, just plain black tea with a ton of lemon. He said the sugar made you crash harder. He ended up moving out to Arizona, said the dry heat was better for his joints. I don't know how anyone can stand living in a desert, honestly. All that sand and those cactus things... what do they call them? Saguaro? Yeah, those big ones with the arms. 

But anyway, yeah, I'm just so tired all the time now. Even just doing small chores, like loading my tools into the back of the truck, it just feels like it's way too much effort. I look at my toolbelt and I just can't even fathom picking it up.

doctor.intent: determine presence of suicidal thoughts

It's awful to say out loud, but sometimes I even catch myself thinking that my wife and my family might actually be better off without me dragging them down. Which really scares me, to be honest. I've never been the kind of guy to think like that. My dad, he was a tough old bird, Korean War vet. He used to say that a man's job was to stand strong no matter what the wind was doing. He had this old oak tree in the front yard that got hit by lightning back in '85. Split right down the middle, but half of it kept growing anyway. He refused to cut it down. Said it earned the right to stay. The city kept sending him letters about it being a hazard, but he just threw them right in the trash. He was stubborn like that. We used to sit under that half-tree and he'd tell me stories about his unit. But... yeah, those thoughts about not waking up, they've been creeping in and it just doesn't feel like me at all.

Slow-cooks it all day with carrots and potatoes. The secret, she says, is searing the meat first in a cast iron skillet. We've had that same skillet since we got married thirty years ago. Found it at a garage sale for five bucks. Best five bucks I ever spent. The guy selling it was moving out to Florida to retire. Had a whole collection of vintage fishing gear he was trying to get rid of, too. I almost bought a bamboo fly rod from him, but I've never really been much of a fisherman. Always seemed like too much sitting around waiting for something to happen. I prefer working with my hands, you know? Making something solid. But yeah, to answer your question, no, my weight hasn't changed or anything like that.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you had any difficulty concentrating or making decisions over the past two months?

patient.answer: Yeah, it's been real tough. I'll be looking at blueprints, right? Blueprints I've read my whole life, same kind of schematics I've been working off of for thirty years. And the lines just blur together in my head. I can't make heads or tails of it. I end up having to ask the younger guys on the crew to repeat things I should understand right away. It's embarrassing, really. Speaking of the younger guys, we got this new kid, Mike. Good kid, but he wears these bright neon yellow work boots. I don't know where he found them, but you can see him coming from a mile away. I told him he looks like a walking traffic cone, but he says they're the most comfortable boots he's ever owned. He actually bought them online. I don't trust buying shoes online, you know? You gotta try them on, walk around the store a bit, make sure they don't pinch your toes. My wife buys all her shoes online now, but she's always having to send them back because they don't fit right. It just seems like a hassle to me, boxing them back up, taking them to the post office... the line at our post office is always out the door. But anyway, yeah, my brain just feels like it's in a fog, can't focus on the plans at all.

He wanted this fancy stamped concrete, paid a fortune for it. Well, the kid running the screed board tripped and I had to jump right in the mix to catch it before he ruined the grade. Ruined a perfectly good pair of Red Wing boots. You can't just wash that stuff off once it starts to cure, you know, it just eats right through the leather. I tried taking them to a cobbler, this old Italian guy downtown, but he just took one look and laughed at me. His shop smelled amazing, though, like shoe polish and strong espresso. He had this antique brass cash register that must have weighed two hundred pounds. But anyway, yeah, if I'm not moving in slow motion, it's the other way around. I'll just get stuck pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands together over and over, and not actually doing anything useful at all.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of psychomotor agitation
doctor.question: Have you been feeling restless or fidgety lately?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: People at the job have noticed I either move like my boots are full of wet cement, taking forever to pick up a board, or I get stuck pacing around the shop rubbing my hands and not actually doing anything useful.

Speaking of my hands, though, my knuckles have been absolutely killing me lately. I think it's the weather changing. We had that huge cold front move in last Tuesday. Reminds me of the winter of '14. Man, it got so cold that year the pipes actually froze solid in our main shop. We had to rent these massive propane torpedo heaters just to keep the guys from freezing to death. You gotta be real careful with those things, though, if you don't ventilate right. My buddy Dave used to run one in his garage with the door shut tight, gave himself mild carbon monoxide poisoning. He's fine now, but they kept him overnight at the hospital for observation. He complained the whole time about the food. Said they just gave him green Jell-O and a piece of dry meatloaf. I never understood why hospitals always push Jell-O on you. Is it supposed to be medicinal or something? My wife makes this cherry Jell-O mold for Thanksgiving with the little mandarin oranges inside, but that's a whole different ballgame. 

But yeah, to answer you, it's just like I mentioned before—I get stuck in that pacing rut, just fidgeting and walking in circles instead of working.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of guilt or shame
doctor.question: Have you been feeling guilty about anything in particular lately?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep replaying every appointment and every change in my wife’s health, telling myself a better husband would have caught it sooner or protected her somehow.

Yeah, I have. I mean, it's just heavy on my chest all the time. I keep replaying every single doctor's appointment, every little change in my wife's health... I just keep telling myself that a better husband would have caught it sooner, you know? Like I should have protected her somehow. 

We used to go to this doctor, Dr. Henderson. Nice guy, had these old Norman Rockwell paintings in his waiting room. I always liked the one with the kid at the soda fountain. You don't see soda fountains anymore, do you? When I was a kid, my granddad used to take me to the pharmacy down on Main Street and they had a real marble counter. We'd get these cherry phosphates. Best thing I ever tasted. Granddad was a carpenter, too, actually. Taught me how to hold a hammer when I was just five years old. He built this incredible oak dining table for my grandmother that we still have in our house. Weighs an absolute ton. We tried moving it when we repainted the dining room last spring, and I swear I almost threw my back out. We painted it this color called "Sea Salt," which my wife picked out. She loves those coastal colors. Reminds her of our honeymoon in Cape Cod. We ate so much lobster on that trip I thought I was gonna turn red. 

But yeah, I just... I can't stop thinking that if I'd paid closer attention, maybe she wouldn't be going through all this, and it's my fault I didn't see the signs.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I think I already mentioned that a minute ago, didn't I? The guys at the site are always on my case about it. They say I'm moving like my boots are full of wet cement, like it takes me forever just to pick up a single piece of lumber. 

Speaking of lumber, the price of pine has gone absolutely through the roof lately. I went down to the supplier last week, and I couldn't believe it. I told the guy, "Are these boards lined with gold?" He just laughed, but it's no joke when you're trying to bid a job. Used to be you could build a whole deck for what they're charging for a stack of two-by-fours now. My buddy Frank builds these massive wrap-around porches out in the county, and he's had to start using this composite decking material instead. It looks okay, I guess, but it doesn't have the same feel as real wood. Real wood has a soul, you know? You can smell the sap when you cut into it. My grandfather used to say you could tell a lot about a man by how he treated his tools and his timber. He kept his chisels so sharp you could shave with them. He had this old leather strop hanging by his workbench... 

But anyway, yeah, they say I'm talking and moving way slower than normal. Unless I'm doing the opposite and just pacing around the shop rubbing my hands together, getting absolutely nothing done.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of psychomotor agitation or retardation to differentiate between F32.1 and F32.2
doctor.question: Have you been feeling like you're moving more quickly than usual, or like your thoughts are racing?

target_item.name: Increased_Activity

target_item.reason: The doctor's question about moving more quickly than usual and having racing thoughts targets the manic/hypomanic symptom of increased energy and activity, which matches this symptom's manifestation of running on a surge, not being able to sit still, and rapidly shifting between ideas and tasks.

patient.answer:
Yeah, well, before this whole cement-boots feeling set in, I had this crazy surge going on. I literally could not sit still. I was up late into the night, just sketching out all these new workshop ideas, calling up suppliers, and hunting for the next thing to fix before I had even finished the first project. 

Speaking of sketching, I still use those old-school yellow Dixon Ticonderoga pencils. Number twos. You know the ones? The eraser on those things is actually decent. Most pencils nowadays, the eraser just smudges the graphite everywhere and ruins the paper. I buy them by the gross from this little office supply store downtown. The guy who runs it, Mr. Higgins, he’s been there since the eighties. He’s got this massive collection of vintage typewriters in the back of the shop. Really beautiful machines. Underwood, Royal, Smith Corona. He let me type on this 1930s Underwood once, and the keys take so much force to press down, your fingers actually get a workout. Makes you appreciate modern keyboards, even if they feel cheap and plasticky. My grandson has this mechanical keyboard for his computer games that lights up in all these crazy rainbow colors. Looks like a disco in his bedroom. I don't get the appeal of playing games in the dark like that, honestly. It's gotta be terrible for your eyes. My mom used to yell at me for reading comics by flashlight under the covers when I was a kid... 

But anyway, yeah. I was just running on that surge, jumping from one fix-it job to the next without finishing anything.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I'd say it is. It's just... I can't focus on the work anymore. I've actually had to hand off parts of jobs that I normally supervise myself, which is hard for me because I like things done a certain way. 

Like when we're framing a house, if the studs aren't perfectly plumb, it throws off the drywall, and then the baseboards don't sit right. It's a whole domino effect. I learned that from this old foreman I worked under when I was first starting out, guy named Sal. Sal was a character. Always had an unlit cigar in his mouth, just chewing on it all day long. Said he quit smoking in '85 but missed the feel of it. He drove this beat-up old Ford F-150 that was more rust than metal. The tailgate wouldn't even latch, so he had it held shut with a bungee cord. I remember one time we were driving down I-95 and that cord snapped, and all his empty coffee cups just went flying out the back like confetti. He drank that cheap diner coffee, the kind that tastes like burnt pennies. We used to go to this diner on 4th Street, Tommy's. They had the best meatloaf sandwich I've ever had in my life. Thick slice of meatloaf, melted provolone, crispy onions on toasted sourdough. My wife makes a good meatloaf, but she puts green peppers in hers. I'm not a fan of green peppers. They overpower everything else in the dish, you know?

But yeah, the guilt is just... it's bad. I've pulled away from everyone. Haven't been to church in weeks, ignoring my friends, the neighbors... It got so bad that my wife and the contact from our parish actually got really worried about my safety.

doctor.question: Do you feel like you're a burden to your family and friends most of the time?

target_item.manifestation: I have had thoughts like maybe it would be easier if I did not wake up, and sometimes I catch myself thinking my family might be better off without me, even though that scares me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling like a burden to family and friends, which directly maps to my symptom of thinking my family might be better off without me, covered under thoughts of death or suicidal ideation.

Yeah, I do. I really do. I've been having these thoughts lately, like... maybe it would just be easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. Sometimes I catch myself thinking my wife and the kids might actually be better off without me dragging them down, even though thinking that way really scares me. 

Speaking of sleeping, we bought this new mattress a couple months ago, one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box. You cut the plastic and it just inflates like a life raft. It's supposed to be great for your back, but honestly, I think I liked our old coil spring mattress better. We had that thing for fifteen years. I bought it at this local furniture store that used to be over on Main Street, right next to the old movie theater. The theater shut down back in the nineties, but they still have the marquee up. They used to show double features on Saturdays for three bucks. I took my wife there on our first date, actually. We saw some terrible sci-fi movie about giant ants or something, I don't even remember the name of it. We shared a large popcorn, and she accidentally spilled half of it on the floor when a rat ran across the aisle. She screamed so loud the projectionist actually stopped the film. We still laugh about that. Popcorn at the movies is a total rip-off now anyway. You go in there and they want ten dollars for a bucket of stale corn and fake butter. I started sneaking in my own snacks in my coat pockets. The kids think it's embarrassing, but I refuse to pay those prices. My daughter, she's in college now, she told me they check your bags at the door at the theater near her campus...

But yeah, I do feel like a burden. Thinking they'd be better off if I wasn't around, it just... it creeps in, you know?

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Would you say your feelings of worthlessness are present nearly every day?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep replaying every appointment and every change in my wife’s health, telling myself a better husband would have caught it sooner or protected her somehow.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about my feelings of worthlessness and their frequency, which corresponds to the Worthlessness/Guilt symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah, pretty much every day. It's like this heavy weight, you know? I just... I keep replaying every single doctor's appointment, every little change in my wife’s health over the last few years. I keep telling myself that a better husband would have caught it sooner, or... or protected her somehow. 

She used to love going to those antique fairs on the weekends before she got sick. We'd drive out to the county fairgrounds, usually on a Sunday morning. The traffic out there on Route 9 is always a nightmare because of the farmers' market they set up right off the highway. People just slam on their brakes to turn in for fresh tomatoes. I don't get it, honestly. You can buy perfectly good tomatoes at the Stop & Shop down the street. Although, I will say, the supermarket tomatoes always taste kind of watery compared to the ones my grandfather used to grow. He had this massive garden in his backyard. Grew tomatoes, cucumbers, zucchini the size of baseball bats. He used to make his own pickles in these giant glass jars he kept in the cellar. The cellar always smelled like dill and damp earth. I hated going down there as a kid because there were these huge wolf spiders that would hang out near the water heater. I’m still terrified of spiders. Last week I saw one in the garage near my workbench, right next to my circular saw. I actually left the garage and didn't go back in for two days. My son had to come over and kill it for me. He laughed at me, of course. Kids always think they're tougher than their old man once they hit their twenties...

But yeah, the worthlessness... it's there every day. Just constantly thinking I failed her when she needed me most.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely. Like I was saying before, I just... I can't focus on the work anymore. I've actually had to hand off parts of jobs that I normally supervise myself. And at home, I've just pulled away from everyone. Haven't been to church in weeks, ignoring my friends, the neighbors... It got so bad that my wife and the contact from our parish actually got really worried about my safety. 

It's funny, the guy from the parish, Father Mike, he used to be a carpenter too before he joined the priesthood. He's always asking me about the wood I use. He loves cherry wood. Personally, I think cherry is a little too soft for most structural stuff, but it finishes beautifully if you're making cabinets or something. I built a cherry wood hutch for my wife for our tenth anniversary. Took me three months of working weekends in the garage. I used this special tung oil finish that really brought out the grain. Tung oil is great, but it takes forever to dry. You have to apply a coat, wait twenty-four hours, sand it with steel wool, and then do it all over again. I think I put six coats on that hutch. The smell of the oil lingered in the garage for weeks. It kind of smells like roasted nuts, which I didn't mind, but the dog hated it. We had a Golden Retriever back then, Buster. Best dog in the world. He used to sleep under my workbench while I was out there. He hated thunderstorms, though. One time, the thunder was so loud he tried to hide under my truck and got himself stuck. I had to jack up the back end just to get him out... 

But yeah, I'm just not functioning right now. Work, home, it's all just falling apart.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Do you feel like your symptoms have been consistently worse over the past two weeks?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depression has been dragging on for about six months now, long enough that it no longer feels like just a bad week or ordinary stress.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration and consistency of the depressive symptoms (specifically referencing the 2-week diagnostic criteria), which corresponds to the duration of the depressive episode.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it's been bad for a while now. Not just two weeks. It's been dragging on for about six months now, honestly. It's definitely not just a bad week or normal stress anymore. Six months is a long time to feel like this. 

Six months ago was right around the time the transmission went out on my truck. It's a Ford F-150, 2015 model. Great truck, usually. I bought it used from a guy a few towns over who used it for his landscaping business, so it already had some miles on it, but the engine was solid. Anyway, the transmission just completely gave up on me while I was on the highway. Had to get it towed to this shop my brother-in-law recommended. The mechanic there, this guy named Sal, he's a real character. Always has a cigar stub in his mouth, even when he's under a car. I don't know how he breathes down there. He quoted me three grand to rebuild the transmission. Three grand! I thought about just buying a new truck, but have you seen the prices on new trucks lately? It's highway robbery. They put all these computers and touchscreens in them now. I don't need a touchscreen to haul lumber, you know? I just need a radio and a heater that works. My first truck was an old Chevy C10. Bare bones, manual roll-up windows. If something broke, you could actually fix it yourself with a wrench and some elbow grease. Now you need a computer degree just to change the oil... 

But yeah, the depression. It's been about six months of this heavy feeling. It's just... it's been a long six months.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Would you say that your symptoms have been consistently worse over the past two weeks?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depression has been dragging on for about six months now, long enough that it no longer feels like just a bad week or ordinary stress.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the depressive symptoms (specifically if they have been present for at least two weeks), which corresponds to the depressive episode duration of 6 months in the patient's profile.

patient.answer:
Well, like I was just saying, doc, it's not just the last two weeks. It's been dragging on for about six months now. It's definitely been long enough that it no longer feels like just a bad week or ordinary stress, you know? 

Six months... yeah, that would've been right around the time my crew and I were finishing up the wrap-around deck on the Henderson place. Nice folks, the Hendersons. Mrs. Henderson would always bring us out these big pitchers of iced tea around noon. Not the cheap powdered stuff, either. She brewed it real strong with actual tea bags and put fresh mint in it. Said she grew the mint right there in her kitchen window box. Mint is funny like that, you know, it grows like an absolute weed if you aren't careful. My wife tried planting some in our backyard garden a few years back and it completely took over the whole bed. Choked the life right out of her beefsteak tomatoes. We had to dig up the dirt and start completely over the next spring. I bought this organic compost from a farm stand out in the valley to mix into the soil, and let me tell you, it smelled like absolute death. The dog loved it, though. He got out of the house and rolled right in it while I was grabbing my shovel. Had to give him three baths in the driveway with that oatmeal shampoo just to get the stink out. My back was killing me from leaning over the tub... 

But anyway, yeah, to answer your question, it's been a solid six months of this. Not just the last couple of weeks.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Would you say that your symptoms are severely impairing your ability to function in daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I have had to hand off parts of jobs I normally supervise myself, and I have pulled away from church, friends, and neighbors to the point that my wife and parish contact got worried about my safety.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms are severely impairing the patient's ability to function in daily life, which directly maps to the Functional Impairment symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, doc, I mean... I feel like we're going in circles here a bit, but yes. It's severely impairing everything. Like I mentioned before, I'm handing off jobs at work that I usually supervise myself. I just can't do it. And at home, I've completely pulled away. Haven't been to church, ignoring my friends, the neighbors... My wife and Father Mike got so worried about my safety that they had a whole intervention of sorts. 

Interventions are rough. Reminds me of when my brother-in-law, Gary, had to have an intervention for his gambling problem. This was back in the late nineties. Gary was a good guy, but he got hooked on those riverboat casinos. He'd drive three hours just to play blackjack on a Tuesday night. He lost his boat, his savings, almost lost his house. My sister was a wreck. We all sat around their living room—me, my wife, my sister, and Gary's old high school baseball coach, for some reason. Gary was furious. He stormed out and drove off in his Buick. Those old Buicks, they floated down the road like a boat. You couldn't feel a single bump. I always preferred a stiffer suspension, like on a truck, so you can actually feel the road, you know? You want to know what the tires are doing. If you're hauling a trailer full of drywall, you need to feel if it starts swaying. Drywall is heavy stuff, especially the half-inch fire-rated boards. You don't want to mess around with that... 

But anyway, yeah, the impairment is severe. Work, home, it's all a mess. I'm just not functioning.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of the patient's depressive episode
doctor.question: Would you say that your current state is the worst you've felt in the past two months?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This whole change in my mood and behavior has been going on for about two months, since my wife’s health suddenly declined and our routine changed.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's state over the past two months, which directly relates to the duration of the patient's overall mood and behavior changes.

patient.answer:
Well, to be honest with you doc, this whole... this whole specific change in my mood and my behavior, it's really been going on for about two months now. That's right around the time my wife's health suddenly declined and our whole daily routine just went completely out the window. 

It was a massive adjustment. We were suddenly having to drive back and forth to the medical center downtown for her, and let me tell you, the parking garage at that place is an absolute nightmare. I don't know who engineered it, but they designed it with these incredibly tight corners. I drive a full-size pickup, and trying to maneuver around those concrete pillars is like threading a needle in the dark. I actually scraped the passenger side mirror on one of those bright yellow barricade poles. Left a nasty paint streak right on the mirror housing. 

You know, you can usually get paint transfer like that off with a little rubbing compound and a good microfiber cloth if you catch it early enough. You just gotta use small, tight circular motions. You can't press too hard, though, or you'll burn right through the factory clear coat. A lot of guys make that exact mistake. They go out and buy those cheap orbital buffers from the hardware store and just go to town on their doors, and the next thing you know, they're looking at bare primer. Primer isn't meant to be exposed to the weather like that. It actually absorbs moisture, and then before you know it, you get rust bubbling up from underneath the paint... 

But anyway, yeah. Two months. Ever since her health took that sudden hit and our routine changed, my mood has just been stuck in this state.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms, including a persistent loss of interest in activities, feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and significant impairment in social and occupational functioning, have been present for approximately two months, meeting the criteria for a Major Depressive Disorder. Specifically, the patient's symptoms align with the criteria for F32.2, which indicates a moderate depressive episode with no psychotic symptoms.
